html:
The Lower Umpqua, or Quuiich, are a Native people of the Oregon coast at the mouth of the Umpqua River, around present Reedsport and Winchester Bay. They spoke a dialect of Siuslaw, shared with the Siuslaw people to the north.

They lived by fishing for salmon and lamprey, gathering shellfish and hunting. In 1828 a fight at their river killed most of the trapping party of the American Jedediah Smith. In 1855 they signed a treaty that the US Senate never ratified, and in the 1860s they were held at a reservation at Yachats, where many died. Today they belong to the Confederated Tribes of Coos, Lower Umpqua and Siuslaw Indians, with their seat at Coos Bay.
